author: NorthAF
quote: 0/10 for narrative design, character development, writing, and overall plot. After more than a decade of waiting, this is what Rockstar delivers? An incredibly disappointing game from a studio that used to define the standard for open-world gaming.I genuinely don't know who thought Lucia and Jason were compelling protagonists. Jason might as well be a cardboard cutout standing in the background of every cutscene. He has almost no personality, no backbone, and barely any agency. His entire contribution to the relationship seems to boil down to "yes, dear" whenever Lucia proposes something. Meanwhile, Lucia comes across as an insufferable, toxic girlboss character who constantly dominates the narrative. Their relationship feels forced, the dynamic is painfully one-sided, and neither character comes close to the memorable protagonists Rockstar used to **** this goes much deeper than two badly written characters.Rockstar has been on a downward trajectory since the later GTA 5 Online updates, and GTA 6 feels like the culmination of everything that has gone wrong with the **** creative direction has fundamentally changed. Instead of focusing on the core audience that made this franchise successful, Rockstar seems increasingly obsessed with appealing to everyone except its longtime fans. The shift toward a different, more female-centered creative direction isn't inherently the problem; the problem is sacrificing compelling characters, good writing, and the franchise's identity in the **** used to be unapologetic. It was offensive, outrageous, violent, politically incorrect, and, most importantly, it made fun of EVERYONE. Nobody was safe from its satire. That was the entire **** it feels like Rockstar is carefully deciding which groups can be mocked and which must be protected. Violence feels increasingly sanitized and selectively restricted, while the writing seems more interested in pushing a particular worldview than delivering entertaining, intelligent satire. Instead of trusting players to think for themselves, the game often feels like it's trying to lecture them, particularly younger audiences, while ridiculing people who **** was supposed to challenge social norms, not enforce a new set of **** then there's the technical side. A game this expensive, developed for this long, launching with noticeable bugs and a 30 FPS cap on modern consoles is simply unacceptable to me. We've waited over a decade, and apparently smooth performance is still too much to ask from one of the wealthiest and most successful developers in **** make matters worse, Rockstar continues its frustrating approach to PC players. No PC release alongside consoles, leaving millions of players waiting yet again. After what happened with GTA 5, it's difficult not to see this as another deliberate double-dipping strategy. Release on consoles first, sell the PC version later, and potentially sell another enhanced edition after that. Selling essentially the same game to loyal customers two or even three times has become an incredibly cynical business model.
